newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers hold bullish view - MCM survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers hold bullish view - MCM survey.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers last week demonstrated their faith the rally in U.S. debt markets will continue, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

"Investors (were) holding on to the bullish view," said a MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey. "This group got very interested a while ago for the second-half 1996 slowdown."
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 107.9 percent in the week ended November 18 from 107.7 percent in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 26 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," down from 29 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 28 percent, up from 21 percent in the week ended November 13.
Forty-six percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 50 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.12 percent, against 2.25 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 23 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 23 percent the previous week, while 20 percent underweighted it. The remaining 57 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 53 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 10 percent underweighted them.

Separately, 44 percent of respondents said the Federal Open Market Committee's next move would by an easing of credit, probably in second-quarter 1997. Twenty-eight percent said the Fed would raise rates by the middle of next year, and 28 percent said they did not know what to expect from central bank policymakers.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
